signals.what: Notice that a model has crossed the systemic-risk threshold
signals.quote: the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks after that requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met
signals.public_note: Art. 52(6): the Commission publishes the list of models with systemic risk; the notification itself is not published
signals.note: The threshold is training compute above 10^25 floating point operations (Art. 51(2)).

signals.what: Technical documentation, evaluation results and adversarial testing, on request
signals.quote: the results of its evaluation, which shall contain, at a minimum, the information set out in Annex XI for the purpose of providing it, upon request, to the AI Office and the national competent authorities
signals.public_note: Art. 53(7): treated under the confidentiality of Art. 78
signals.retention: 10 years, kept by the authorised representative (Art. 54(3)(b))

signals.what: Capabilities and limitations, to those who build on the model
signals.quote: make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems

signals.what: Serious incidents
signals.quote: keep track of, document, and report, without undue delay, to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities, relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to address them
signals.note: Art. 3(49): a serious incident is an incident or malfunctioning that leads to death, serious harm to health, disruption of critical infrastructure, infringement of fundamental rights or serious harm to property or the environment.

signals.what: The safety and security framework, to the AI Office
signals.quote: Signatories will provide the AI Office with (unredacted) access to their Framework, and updates thereof, within five business days of either being confirmed.
signals.public_note: Measure 10.2: a summarised version is published only 'if and insofar as necessary'
signals.note: Five business days, counted as seven calendar days. A framework assessment is due at least every 12 months (Measure 1.3).

signals.what: The Model Report: evaluations, risk acceptance and mitigations, before release
signals.quote: Signatories will provide the AI Office with access to the Model Report (without redactions, unless they are required by national security laws to which Signatories are subject) by the time they place a model on the market
signals.public_note: Measure 10.2: a summarised version is published only 'if and insofar as necessary'
signals.note: May be delayed by up to 15 business days with an interim report (counted as 21 calendar days); updated at least every six months for the most capable models.

signals.what: Serious incidents, with timelines
signals.quote: a serious cybersecurity breach, including the (self-)exfiltration of model weights and cyberattacks, or if the Signatories establish or suspect with reasonable likelihood such a causal relationship between their model and the breach, not later than five days after
signals.note: Two days for critical infrastructure, five for a cybersecurity breach, ten for a death, fifteen for other serious harm, each after the Signatory becomes aware of its model's involvement; a self-exfiltration of weights is the model's own act and need not have harmed anyone.

signals.what: Detailed evaluations and mitigations, on request
signals.quote: Signatories will draw up and keep up-to-date the following information for the purpose of providing it to the AI Office upon request:
signals.retention: at least 10 years after the model is placed on the market

signals.what: Reports about serious incidents from users and other third parties
signals.quote: facilitate the reporting of relevant information about serious incidents by downstream modifiers, downstream providers, users, and other third parties to:
signals.receiver_name: the Signatory, or the AI Office

signals.what: Results of risk measures for models above a compute threshold
signals.quote: AI business operators shall submit the results of implementing the measures pursuant to each Subparagraphs of Paragraph 1 to the Minister of Science and ICT.
signals.note: The duty attaches when training compute meets a threshold set by Presidential Decree; when and in what form results are submitted is left to the Minister's guidelines.
signals.doubt: trigger: the text states no occasion

signals.what: Data on request, on suspicion of a violation or a complaint
signals.quote: The Minister of Science and ICT may require that AI business operators submit relevant data or have public officials conduct necessary investigations in any of the following cases:

signals.what: The frontier AI framework, published
signals.quote: publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.
signals.note: Reviewed at least once a year; must cover risks from a model circumventing oversight mechanisms (a policy, not a record of acts).

signals.what: Transparency report with summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments, at release
signals.quote: Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report
signals.note: Redactions allowed for trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety and national security (§ 22757.12(f)).

signals.what: Catastrophic-risk assessments of internal use, every three months
signals.quote: transmit to the Office of Emergency Services a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models every three months
signals.public_note: exempt from the California Public Records Act (§ 22757.13(f))

signals.what: Critical safety incidents
signals.quote: frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering the critical safety incident.
signals.public_note: from 2027-01-01 a yearly report with anonymized and aggregated information, sent to the Legislature and the Governor (§ 22757.13(g))
signals.note: A critical safety incident includes a model's loss of control causing death or injury and a model using deceptive techniques against its developer outside an evaluation; the second needs no harm.

signals.what: Imminent danger, to an authority within a day
signals.quote: developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction
signals.receiver_name: an appropriate authority (law enforcement or public safety)

signals.what: Anyone may report a critical safety incident
signals.quote: establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident
signals.note: The report states the reasons the incident qualifies, so its class says when a model acted.

signals.what: Employees may disclose to the Attorney General
signals.quote: information to the Attorney General, a federal authority, a person with authority over the covered employee, or another covered employee who has authority to investigate, discover, or correct the reported issue
signals.receiver_name: Attorney General or a federal authority
signals.public_note: from 2027-01-01 a yearly anonymized and aggregated report by the Attorney General (§ 22757.14(d))

signals.what: An anonymous internal channel, shared with officers quarterly
signals.quote: provide a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose information to the large frontier developer
signals.note: A monthly update goes to the person who disclosed; disclosures go to officers and directors at least once a quarter.

signals.what: Sharing of vulnerabilities, risks, threats and safety incidents
signals.quote: establish a risk and threat information sharing mechanism that covers developers, service providers, and special technical institutions

signals.what: Public complaints and reports on AI risks
signals.quote: A mechanism for handling public complaints and reports on AI risks and hazards should be established

signals.what: Test reports before commercial use
signals.quote: Developers creating products for commercial use should generate detailed test reports, analyze security issues, and propose improvement plans.

signals.what: Tolerance to interference, to providers and other developers
signals.quote: Assess the tolerance of the AI model and algorithm to external interference and inform service providers and other developers of its

signals.what: Regular disclosure of auditing and anomaly handling
signals.quote: Regularly disclose information on the auditing and anomaly handling of AI models and algorithms.

signals.what: Operational logs of system and user activity
signals.quote: Maintain operational logs for large model services, including system and user activities. The logs should be retained for at least six months, and audited regularly.
signals.doubt: machine or person: 'system and user activities' read as an actor distinction; a stricter reader may read ordinary system logging

signals.what: Alert thresholds on operational indicators
signals.quote: Set security alert thresholds for key operational indicators to enable timely detection of incidents.

signals.what: Capabilities, limitations, target users and scenarios, disclosed
signals.quote: Improve the transparency and fairness of AI applications by disclosing their capabilities, limitations, target users, and scenarios.
signals.doubt: trigger: occasion not stated; receiver: 'disclosing' read as public

signals.what: Incident reporting outside the organisation
signals.quote: Externally, it refers to the capability to report incidents to key stakeholders outside an organisation when required or needed. Such stakeholders can include regulatory authorities, users, customers, or value chain participants.
signals.receiver_name: regulators, users, customers or value-chain participants
signals.note: The guide calls a failure an incident when it creates harm of sufficient severity, and asks for a common definition.

signals.what: Information for deployers and end users
signals.quote: providing relevant information to downstream deployers and end users, so that they can make informed decisions about the deployment or use of the Gen AI model or system.

signals.what: Reports of issues and vulnerabilities by users and third parties
signals.quote: facilitating third-party and user discovery and reporting of issues and vulnerabilities after deployment such as through bounty systems, contests, or prizes

signals.what: Transparency reports for every significant release
signals.quote: This should include publishing transparency reports containing meaningful information for all new significant releases of advanced AI systems.

signals.what: Sharing of risks, dangerous capabilities and attempts to circumvent safeguards
signals.quote: Organizations should collaborate with other organizations across the AI lifecycle to share and report relevant information to the public with a view to advancing safety, security and trustworthiness of advanced AI systems.
signals.receiver_name: other organisations, the public, public authorities
signals.note: Among what is shared: 'attempts by AI actors to circumvent safeguards'; in the code's vocabulary AI actors are the people and organisations of the lifecycle, not the systems.
signals.doubt: machine or person: a class of people's acts, which the codebook's 'by class' does not name

signals.what: Governance and risk-management policies, disclosed
signals.quote: Organizations are expected to establish and disclose their AI governance policies and organizational mechanisms to implement these policies

signals.what: Non-sensitive evaluation findings in a shared public repository
signals.quote: we agree to publish the non-sensitive findings of our evaluations in a standardized format to ensure comparability, while also creating a publicly accessible shared repository.

signals.what: Capabilities, limitations and known risks, disclosed
signals.quote: Commit to disclose model capabilities, limitations, and known risks
signals.doubt: trigger: occasion not stated; receiver: 'disclose' read as public

signals.what: Timely sharing of AI control incidents and precursor signals
signals.quote: share timely information on serious cyber and AI control incidents and other material precursor signals of serious harm, whether it's between companies and government, between governments or between AI companies
signals.note: The signatories commit to align on incident classification; none is given.

signals.what: Confidential channels for whistleblowers
signals.quote: Policy makers commit to offer secure and confidential channels through which whistleblowers, including employees and other relevant stakeholders, can raise concerns about systemic risks

signals.what: Real-time monitoring of emergent capabilities and internal reporting lines
signals.quote: real-time monitoring of emergent capabilities, rigorous internal red-teaming, and transparent reporting lines that protect internal researchers

signals.what: The frontier AI framework, published
signals.quote: publish the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within thirty days.

signals.what: Transparency report at release
signals.quote: Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a transparency report

signals.what: Catastrophic-risk assessments of internal use, every three months
signals.quote: A large frontier developer shall transmit to the office a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models every three months
signals.receiver_name: office in the Department of Financial Services

signals.what: Critical safety incidents within 72 hours
signals.quote: report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the office within seventy-two hours from a determination that a critical safety incident has occurred
signals.receiver_name: office in the Department of Financial Services
signals.public_note: from 2028-01-01 a yearly report with anonymized and aggregated information, sent to the Governor and legislative leaders (§ 1422(7))

signals.what: Imminent danger, to an authority within a day
signals.quote: the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within twenty-four hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction
signals.receiver_name: an appropriate authority (law enforcement or public safety)

signals.what: Anyone may report a critical safety incident
signals.quote: The office shall establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier developer or a member of the public to report a critical safety incident
signals.receiver_name: office in the Department of Financial Services

signals.what: Disclosure statement before developing or deploying, renewed every two years
signals.quote: no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part in New York state, without having a current disclosure statement filed with the office
signals.receiver_name: office in the Department of Financial Services
signals.public_note: the office publishes the list of developers who filed, without contacts (§ 1428(6)); the statement itself is not published

signals.what: Monthly reports of chip exports to US-headquartered users
signals.quote: Reports regarding any export, reexport, or transfer (incountry) subject to the provisions of this section are due no later than the first business day of the month following the transaction.
signals.note: Each report names the parties and, per product, its total processing performance and quantity. Due by the first business day of the next month, counted as at most 33 days.

signals.what: Notice to the recipient that data-centre use for listed firms needs a licence
signals.quote: the exporter, reexporter, or transferor must inform the recipient that a BIS authorization is required if the item or items will be used at a data center to provide access to more than 12,000,000

signals.what: Yearly reports under a validated end-user authorisation
signals.quote: reports are due by February 15 of each year, and must cover the period from January 1 through December 31 of the prior year.
signals.note: From 46 days (a transfer on 31 December) to 410 days (on 1 January).

signals.what: Records of an agent's actions and of human interventions
signals.quote: Maintaining records of relevant decisions, actions, tool calls, inputs, outputs and human interventions sufficient to support oversight, investigation and accountability.
signals.note: The resolution names the difficulty itself: an agent's delegated authority can make it hard to tell a user's acts from the agent's.

signals.what: Monitoring and reporting of unexpected behaviour after deployment
signals.quote: measures should be in place to monitor for and report on unexpected behaviors or failures.
signals.note: The receiver of the report is not named.

signals.what: An inventory of approved agent systems
signals.quote: maintaining an up-to-date inventory of approved systems and their purposes, models, tools, skills, data sources, connections and permissions
